reason: E2 directly demonstrates that faster pyrolysis (FMBP) yields homogeneous NiPdPt alloy while slower methods cause phase segregation, supporting the core kinetic-freezing premise. E1 and E3 provide general context that thermal shock can freeze high-entropy states and that slow kinetics cause segregation, but neither directly confirms the specific burst nucleation/supersaturation mechanism or the noble-metal boundary condition.
premises: Rapid simultaneous precursor decomposition creates high supersaturation of metal atoms
High supersaturation triggers burst nucleation that kinetically freezes a mixed state
Rapid cooling suppresses diffusion-driven segregation, locking in a homogeneous alloy
Slower heating leads to sequential reduction and phase-separated or core–shell structures
